title: Scoped read gating: tenant-scope without tier block, and bound-partition probing
summary: How to add a protected root to the io-layer read gate without breaking legit readers: apply checkTenantScope but skip the tier block, and teach every enumerator to probe <tier>/<bound> instead of listing the tier root.
procedure_steps: (1) validateReadPermission and checkTenantScope are separable: adding a path to the protected set gives you cross-tenant denial for free; the personaTierReadDecision tier block is a second, wider gate you can keep off. (2) Denial is invisible to enumeration: safeExistsSync swallows ROLE_VIOLATION into false and safeLstat/safeReaddir throw — a bound process cannot list a tier root, so every enumerator must probe <tier>/<bound> directly or silently see nothing. (3) Bound identities must not enumerate tenant lists — same rule as knowledge/confidential/; probing your own partition is the legitimate equivalent. (4) Caches over scope-relative views must key by the binding (bound tenant here), or a narrowed view satisfies a wider later lookup. (5) Owner-scope visibility already filters to the bound tenant, so bound-partition probing is not a behavior change — only the io contract catches up.
